title: Ife copper-alloy heads
summary: Naturalistic heads cast in brass and copper by the lost-wax method at Ife, in south-western Nigeria, dated by sources between the 11th and 15th centuries. Workmen digging house foundations in the Wunmonije Compound in January 1938 found 17 of them, and their publication in 1938-9 created a sensation in the western world.

uncertainty.note: The British Museum Images page gives "probably 12th-14th century AD" in its title line and "14thC-15thC(early) (probably)" in its production date; World History Encyclopedia gives 11th to 15th century CE from chemical analysis. Range here is the span of the heads, not one head.

when.display: 11th to 15th century CE (British Museum: probably 14th to early 15th century)

importance.justification: The British Museum calls the Ife sculptures one of the highest achievements of African art and culture.

reviewer_note: Counts differ: the British Museum says 17 heads plus the upper half of a king figure; World History Encyclopedia says twelve heads were found together. Summary uses the British Museum count. No opened source gives a coordinate for Wunmonije Compound, so the pin is Ile-Ife city.
